_comment: THE single hand-edited source for the portal's visual tokens.
Everything else is generated from this file by tools/gen_tokens.py:
frontend/src/styles/tokens.css  — the React path, imported by base.css
backend/tokens.py               — the Python path, injected by shell.BASE_CSS
frontend/src/lib/tokens.ts      — for colours that must reach JS (recharts
props, inline styles, score bands)
Those three are GENERATED. Edit this file and re-run the generator instead;
tests/test_design_tokens.py fails if they drift.
Token NAMES are deliberately the ones already in use (--bg, --acc, --c-pr...),
not the Constructor Fabric --color-* names. Renaming is a separate, visible
step — see docs/design-system.md. This file exists so that step is one edit.
`themes` is a map so a dark theme is additive: add a `dark` key with the same
token names and the generator emits its block too. Absent today.
`text_on` names the surfaces a colour is used as BODY TEXT on. The contrast
test derives its WCAG AA pairs from it. Non-text use (icons, borders, chart
fills) is not asserted yet.
VALUES ARE VERBATIM what shipped before consolidation. Several are near-
duplicates that a design pass should collapse, and they are kept apart here
because collapsing them changes pixels:
#8b5cf6 lives under four names: --app, --violet, --c-loc, --c-epic, --cat-task
--acc-soft #edecfe and --acc-bg #eeeefe are two lavenders one apart
chart/* and category/* overlap on five hues but disagree on epic
See docs/design-system.md for the list and why each is still separate.

panel2.note: inset surface — code, table head, chips

mut.note: muted text — labels, meta. Darkened 2026-08-03 from #8a93a3, which was 2.73:1 on --panel2 — below AA even for large text — across 223 uses.

on-solid.note: text/icons on a SATURATED fill (--acc, --good, --bad). In dark this flips to near-black, because a dark theme's fills are lighter than the page.

tooltip-fg.note: text on --tooltip-bg. Split from --on-solid on 2026-08-03: both were white in light, but on a dark surface the two requirements are opposite.

bad-soft.note: the failed-to-load card's fill (set from TS)

acc-bg.note: accent surface, identity page's one-off shade

star.note: rating star, calibrate page. Darkened 2026-08-03 from #f5a623 (2.03:1). The bar is 3:1, not 4.5: a star is a rating CONTROL, so WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast applies.

violet.note: computed-metric accent. Darkened 2026-08-03 from #8b5cf6 (3.63:1 on its own pill).

chg-design.note: changelog 'design' category (was a second --app). Darkened 2026-08-03 from #8250df (4.17:1 on its own pill).

swatch-empty.note: a work-type with no colour set yet

company-empty.note: a company with no colour pinned or derived

chart._split_note: --app and --c-bug are chart FILLS that were also used as text, where they measured 4.23:1 and 3.76:1. Darkening the fill would repaint every chart, so the text use got its own token. Fills below keep their hue; use --app-fg / --c-bug-fg for type.

c-bug-fg.note: --c-bug as TEXT (the 'required' marker, a gap cell)

category._note: The taxonomy wizard's work-category swatches — a SEPARATE palette from chart/*, consumed by name from SemanticWizard.tsx. It agrees with chart/* on five hues and disagrees on epic (#5b5bf0 here, #8b5cf6 there); that disagreement predates this file and is preserved rather than silently resolved.

status._note: Badge, pill and row surfaces. These are the pre-redesign GitHub-ish semantic pairs, and they are NOT the same values as --good/--good-bg etc — a pill's green surface (#dafbe1) and the card's (#e7f6ee) have always differed. Kept apart because unifying them changes pixels; unifying is a step-5 design call.

exp-fg.note: Darkened 2026-08-03 from #c77700, which was 3.13:1 on the badge fill. --exp-bg is amber at 13% alpha, compositing to #fef2de over a card, so the fill is far lighter than its hex suggests.

tooltip-bg.note: tooltip and log surfaces — dark even in the light theme, so its text is --tooltip-fg, not --on-solid

chat-tool-bg.note: tool-call block in the chat log

option-fg.note: native <option> text, which ignores most inherited colour

score._note: Developer-score bands (widgets/score/PersonScore). Read from TS, never from CSS.

space._note: The Constructor Fabric 4px grid. Used for LAYOUT spacing — page and card padding, section margins, gaps. Micro-spacing below 14px is deliberately still literal: this UI has a lot of 1-3px padding on pills, chips and legend swatches, and snapping those to a 4px step is a density redesign rather than a grid migration. 38px+ is also literal — the kit's scale stops at 32px, and the values above it (46, 64, 90, 130) are specific layout measures, not steps.

radius._note: The Constructor Fabric scale (6/8/12/16) plus two steps it does not define but this UI needs: `r-xs` for sub-6px details (legend swatches, thin progress bars) and `r-pill` for fully-rounded chips. Before 2026-08-03 there were 16 distinct literal radii; they were mapped onto this scale by ROLE, not by arithmetic — controls onto `r-md` to match the kit's buttons, and `.pill`/`.tag` off a 20px radius that already exceeded half their height onto `r-pill`, which is visually identical.

r-sm.note: inline code, small chip. WAS 12px until 2026-08-03 — every var(--r-sm) was remapped to --r-lg in the same commit.

shadow._note: ONE elevation, matching the Constructor Fabric kit: it defines a single `Elevation subtle` (0 8px 24px at 28% black) for floating or focused surfaces and states that standard cards rely on BORDERS. Until 2026-08-03 there were two shadows and they sat on every card and every button, which is what made the UI read as uniformly lifted. The 37 resting cards that also had a border simply lost the shadow; the two borderless controls (.pseg, .scope-select) gained the border the kit prescribes rather than a second, subtler shadow that would have reintroduced the thing being removed.

dark._note: Dark theme. Surfaces and --ink are chosen; every other chromatic value is DERIVED from its light counterpart by keeping hue and saturation and raising lightness until it clears its declared text_on / graphic_on pairs against the dark surfaces (tools/gen_tokens.py has no part in this — see the derivation script referenced in docs/design-system.md). Note what deriving means for a RAMP: it stops at the lowest lightness that clears the target, so two tokens with different requirements can still land on the same floor. --ink2 (5.15 on --panel) and --mut (5.14) do exactly that and are currently indistinguishable from each other; --ink is chosen precisely so the top of the ramp does not join them. Tokens ABSENT here deliberately inherit the light value: chart/*, category/* and score/* are fills chosen for mutual distinguishability, which does not change with the page colour, and radius/* is geometry. --on-solid FLIPS to near-black, because a dark theme's saturated fills are lighter than the page, so dark text on them is what passes.

ink.note: CHOSEN, not derived — see the _note above. Was #6e8bc5 until 2026-08-04: derive_dark_theme.py picks #e7eaf0 for the ink ramp and then its generic text_on loop overwrote it, landing every text token on the same 4.5:1 floor. --ink measured 5.11 on --panel against --ink2's 5.15 and --mut's 5.14, so primary, secondary and muted text were indistinguishable and primary was nominally the weakest of the three. It was also blue, because the loop preserves the hue of #101828 — a near-black, where hue means nothing until lightness is raised.

_chart_contrast_note: 2026-08-03: four hues were darkened so a chart mark clears 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11) on BOTH page colours, which a payload colour has to do since the server does not know the theme. #f59e0b was 2.15:1 on white, #10b981 2.54, #06b6d4 2.43, #14b8a6 2.49 — they read as pale washes on a light background. Now #ce8508 / #0fa976 / #05a3be / #12a796, each 3.0 light and 5.8 dark. Applied by VALUE across every group and palette, so the same hue stays one hue wherever it appears.

palettes._note: Colours handed out in code rather than referenced from CSS — a chart series' `color` in an API payload, a score band, an index-assigned swatch. Both the frontend (lib/tokens.ts) and the backend (backend/tokens.py VALUES/palettes) read these from here. A list's ORDER is load-bearing: it decides which colour something gets by index, so appending is safe and reordering repaints existing items.

company_palette._note: Company series colours, assigned by a name-derived hash (store.company_color_map) so a company keeps its colour as ranks change. The teal was #0a7ea4, which sat 58 units from the blue in RGB — close enough that two adjacent series read as one colour; it became #14b8a6, 95 from its nearest neighbour, and then #12a796 when the palette was darkened for legibility on white.

series_colors._note: One-off named series in specific charts. The frontend legend swatches in Trend.tsx read `opened`/`merged` from here, so both sides share one entry instead of two hand-matched literals. These are PAYLOAD colours: the server picks them without knowing the client's theme, so each has to work on both. `total` was #1f2328 — near-black, chosen for a white page, and 1.10:1 on the dark surface, i.e. invisible. It is now a neutral that clears 3:1 both ways (4.19 light / 4.16 dark). Every value here now clears 3:1 on both page colours; see _chart_contrast_note above for the four that did not.

on_primary._comment: Foreground used on a filled --acc surface. Checked by the contrast test.
